title: Replicating the FLI AI Safety Index for Chinese AI Labs

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: assessing Chinese lab governance fills a critical blind spot in the global safety landscape. Any governance regime excluding China covers only a fraction of frontier development.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires Chinese language skills, understanding of Chinese regulatory context (MIIT standards, AI governance rules), and the ability to navigate non-Western documentation norms.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: 5-6 labs in a fundamentally different regulatory context with language barriers makes this very ambitious for 30 hours by beginner CS students.

novelty.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2025 already includes two Chinese companies: Zhipu AI and DeepSeek, both receiving failing overall grades. The index acknowledges that Chinese corporate governance norms differ and that China has its own AI regulations reducing reliance on self-governance. Concordia AI published 'The State of AI Safety in China' (Spring 2024) and the Turing Institute's CETAS published 'Seeking Deeper: Assessing China's AI Security Ecosystem.' The EA Forum 'China x AI Reference List' (August 2025 update) catalogs extensive resources. While extending the FLI methodology to additional Chinese labs (Baidu, ByteDance, Alibaba) would add coverage, the core methodological question of applying Western governance frameworks to Chinese labs is already explored. The language barrier and regulatory context challenges are documented.

evidence: FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2025 (includes Zhipu AI and DeepSeek).
